subject: GraniteWorks site acceptance: on-prem K8s topology, NVMe binding & egress gating
messages:
From: Eli Stone <eli.stone@graniteworks.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyanka Shah <pri.shah@graniteworks.com>
Date: 2025-04-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [GraniteWorks] Site acceptance + NVMe binding question

Aditya / Marissa —

Thanks for the call earlier. We attached the site inventory (CSV) and a rough rack map. Two immediate asks before we lock the acceptance window:

1) We need a short checklist for cluster requirements (control plane HA, kubelet Taints, minimum node sizing) that our data center ops can sign off on.
2) Our hardware team insists that certain NVMe bays be reserved for local scratch vs. persistent blockstore. We need Redwood guidance on binding persistent volumes to particular host devices or whether to rely on a CSI-level abstraction.
3) egress: firewall team requires candidate public egress IPs and a BGP plan for outbound traffic.

Can you respond with a short deployable checklist and highlight any gating items that might block the go/no-go on our side?

We'd like to target the first onsite install window the week of May 12, pending your acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Eli Stone
Infra PM — GraniteWorks

Attachments: granite-inventory-20250407.csv, rack_map_sketch.jpg
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Eli Stone <eli.stone@graniteworks.com>, Priyanka Shah <pri.shah@graniteworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [GraniteWorks] Site acceptance + NVMe binding question

Eli / Priyanka —

Thanks for the inventory. High level reply and a deploy checklist below. I kept it pragmatic so your ops team can baseline quickly. I'll follow up with a one-page diagram and a sample CSI patch we recommend.

Topline cluster requirements (minimal, for Redwood Private serving LLM inference):
- Control plane: 3 control-plane VMs (dedicated) across two racks if possible; prefer odd-quorum. Each control-plane: 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM, 200GB boot.
- Etcd: co-located on control-plane nodes, recommend encrypted disks and isolated NICs for etcd traffic.
- Worker nodes: 3 nodepools to start:
  * inference-large: 8 x GPU nodes (A100 / H100 equivalent) — 48 vCPU, 384GB RAM, local NVMe for model cache (see binding notes)
  * inference-small: 4 x CPU-only for agent tasks / telemetry — 16 vCPU, 64GB RAM, ephemeral SSD
  * infra/system: 3 x medium nodes for logging, monitoring, and CSI controllers — 16 vCPU, 64GB RAM
- Node taints: inference nodes: dedicated=true:NoSchedule; infra nodes: infra=true:NoExecute for system-critical pods.
- Pod density: plan for ~8 heavy inference pods per GPU node with dynamic batch sizing.

Storage & NVMe binding guidance:
- Recommended pattern: use a CSI that supports node affinity + volumeTopologies (we use abstraction, not raw device mapping). Do NOT bake PVs to physical bay numbers; instead provision by host-local directory for scratch and CSI-backed blockstore for persistent model shards.
- For model cache (hot NVMe): configure hostPath-backed cache service with explicit file-system path (e.g., /var/local/nvme/cache) and nodeSelectors for inference-large pool. This gives predictable locality without brittle device mapping.
- For persistent volumes (model shards, checkpoints): use the CSI blockstore with volume replication if you need durability; bind to a storageClass that is limited to nodes in inference-large via allowedTopologies. That ensures volumes are created only on desired hosts.
- Gating: if ops cannot expose allowedTopologies or cannot guarantee node label stability, we will fallback to networked blockstore (slower).

Networking & egress:
- Control plane & API: place control-plane on a management VLAN with ACLs from your corp mgmt subnets.
- Pod egress: we require a small set of egress IPs for telemetry, license checks, and model downloads (~5 IPs). If you prefer BGP, advertise a /29 from your border and we'll accept outbound mapping; otherwise we can NAT to a fixed pool.
- BGP note: prefer static route + NAT if ops prefers simpler setup. BGP gives lower latency for cross-region fallbacks but requires peering windows.
- Firewall gating: we will provide a minimal egress allowlist (TCP 443 to our model registries, TCP 5222 for heartbeat, and traceroute/ICMP optional).

Acceptance checklist (ops sign-off):
1) Rack inventory validated & power redundancy confirmed.
2) VLANs and mgmt subnet provisioned for control-plane; at least one /27 for node IPs.
3) Node labels and kubelet config agreed (taints, runtimeClass, kubelet eviction thresholds).
4) NVMe devices presented and mounted on inference-large nodes at /var/local/nvme (ops to confirm mount stable on reboot).
5) CSI storageClass created with allowedTopologies for inference-large (ops to have CAPABILITY to restrict topology).
6) Egress IPs / BGP peering decision and firewall rules in place.
7) KMS key material available for disk encryption (optional but required for SOC2 workflow).

Action items & owners:
- Redwood (Aditya): prepare one-page NVMe-binding diagram + sample CSI policy (ETA 2025-04-09).
- GraniteWorks (Eli): confirm whether you can provide allowedTopologies and if mountpoints can be enforced (ETA 2025-04-10).
- GraniteWorks (Priyanka): share firewall change window and decision on BGP vs NAT (ETA 2025-04-09).
- Redwood (Neha): will review SOC2 evidence needs once topology stabilized.

If nothing blocks, we can confirm the May 12 install window.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Lead Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0192

Date: 2025-04-09T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [GraniteWorks] Site acceptance + NVMe binding question

On Wed, Apr 8, 2025 at 11:03 AM Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> If ops cannot expose allowedTopologies or cannot guarantee node label stability, we will fallback to networked blockstore (slower).

Thanks Aditya — two quick clarifications from the SRE team:
- We can provide node labels and mount points, but our provisioning system occasionally re-images nodes which can change device naming. We prefer an approach that does not rely on /dev/nvmeX device names.
- For egress, we can NAT through your suggested /29. BGP peering will add operational overhead for us; we'll keep that as opt-in.

Also, SOC2: our security team will need the disk encryption details and a list of logs that Redwood will ship to our logging endpoint. Neha — can you send the minimal evidence list we need to present to our auditors?

We can commit to the May 12 window provided the checklist items (especially NVMe mount stability and firewall window) are met.

—Priyanka (SRE)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <pri.shah@graniteworks.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-10T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [GraniteWorks] Site acceptance + NVMe binding question

Priyanka / Eli —

Short SOC2 evidence checklist for the acceptance packet (minimal set we typically ask customers to collect):
- KMS integration: confirmation of key IDs and rotation policy (screenshot or KMS ARN).
- Host inventory: signed CSV (you already attached) plus confirmation of mountpoints (ops to confirm).
- Network ACLs & egress: firewall rule snapshot showing allowed egress IPs and ports.
- Audit logs: 30 days of control-plane and API-server audit logs will be required during the on-site acceptance window. If you cannot retain 30 days prior, please ensure we have audit-forwarding enabled for the first 30 days post-install.
- Access control: list of users with cluster-admin during acceptance; we require a temporary expiring admin token policy.

If you can provide the above items by 2025-04-13 we'll prepare the formal acceptance doc and the SOW will be updated to lock May 12.

I'll attach a short template for the evidence packet (see attachment: sow-granite-draft-v2.pdf).

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
